[Obesity in adults - Canadian clinical practice guideline (Wharton et al., CMAJ 2020) > Canadian adult obesity guideline - summary]
- Obesity is defined as a complex, progressive and relapsing chronic disease in which abnormal or excess body fat impairs health. - The guideline shifts the focus of obesity management toward improving patient-centred health outcomes rather than weight loss alone. - Clinicians are asked to move beyond simplistic "eat less, move more" messaging and address root drivers of obesity, while validating patients' lived experience. - It contains 80 key recommendations across 19 chapters, bookended by chapters on weight bias and on the care of Indigenous peoples. - BMI alone is not an accurate tool for identifying adiposity-related complications; combining BMI with waist circumference and clinical assessment is preferred.
